To hobnob with someone means to socialize with them in a friendly, relaxed, and informal way — chatting, mingling, eating, drinking, laughing — essentially spending enjoyable social time together.

But here is the key detail that makes this word special: it almost always describes socializing with people who are important, powerful, wealthy, famous, or of high social status. That is the heart of the word. You do not typically say someone is hobnobbing with their neighbours or coworkers. You say it when someone is mixing with people who are above them socially, or at least who are notable or influential in some way.

Think of it as a combination of two ideas:

1. Casual, friendly socializing — not a formal meeting, not a business transaction, but relaxed mingling. Conversation over drinks, small talk at a party, laughing at a gala, chatting at an exclusive event.

2. With people of status or influence — celebrities, politicians, billionaires, royalty, executives, the elite of a field.

Put them together and you get hobnob: casually rubbing shoulders with important or powerful people.

This is where the word gets interesting. Hobnob carries a mildly ironic or gently mocking tone. When you use it, you are subtly hinting one of two things:

  • The person is name-dropping or showing off — "Look who I was hanging out with!"
  • The person is socializing with people above their usual circle — there is a slight air of social climbing, of someone who is pleased with themselves for gaining access to important company.

It is not a cruel or harsh word at all. It is more like a gentle, slightly amused way of pointing out that someone is enjoying the company of the high and mighty. Sometimes it is affectionate, sometimes slightly teasing, but never insulting.

However, in some contexts it is completely neutral — it simply means socializing with influential people, with no judgment attached.
Structure: how it is used in a sentence

Hobnob is almost always followed by "with" and then the people in question.

  • "She was hobnobbing with celebrities."
  • "He loves to hobnob with politicians."
  • "They spent the evening hobnobbing with the city's wealthiest families."

The subject of the sentence is the one doing the socializing, and the people after "with" are the important/notable ones.

At a film festival:
"A young journalist found herself hobnobbing with Oscar-winning directors at the after-party."
→ She was mingling and chatting casually with famous directors — people well above her in the film world.

In politics:
"The lobbyist spent his career hobnobbing with senators and cabinet ministers."
→ He was constantly socializing in informal settings with powerful government figures.

In business:
"After her startup went public, she began hobnobbing with Silicon Valley billionaires."
→ She was now mixing socially with the elite of the tech world.

With mild mockery:
"Oh, he's too busy hobnobbing with the aristocracy to return my calls."
→ Said with gentle sarcasm — the person is so caught up socializing with important people that he has become unavailable.

Neutral/positive use:
"The conference gave young scientists a rare opportunity to hobnob with Nobel laureates."
→ Simply: a chance to socialize informally with legendary scientists.

• It does not mean a deep, meaningful friendship. It refers to the surface level of socializing — chatting, mingling, attending events together, moving in the same social circles. Two old childhood friends catching up would not be described as hobnobbing.
  • It does not involve any formal or professional interaction. A job interview, a business deal, or a scheduled meeting is not hobnobbing. It is always casual and social in nature.
  • It does not necessarily mean the person is dishonest or manipulative. The word does not accuse anyone of anything — it just describes the social activity, sometimes with a hint of amusement.

If you want one sentence to lock it in your memory:

To hobnob is to socialize casually and comfortably with people of wealth, power, or fame — often with the implication that the person is enjoying or showing off this access to important company.

Whenever you see this word, picture someone at a glamorous party, glass in hand, effortlessly chatting and laughing with influential people — that is hobnobbing.
